summary: Morombe Airport (MXM) is a regional airfield serving the coastal town of Morombe on Madagascar's southwestern coast, along the Mozambique Channel. The airport provides a vital air link for this relatively remote area where road travel can be slow and challenging. It supports regional connectivity, tourism to nearby beaches and Kirindy Forest, and local fishing industry operations.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate from Morombe Airport?
A: Morombe Airport is primarily served by domestic regional carriers operating flights to and from Antananarivo via Toliara, with scheduled services typically running a few times per week.

Q: When is the best time to visit Morombe?
A: The dry season from April to November is generally considered the best time, with cooler temperatures and less rainfall. The cyclone season from January to March can bring heavy rains and storms.

Q: Does Morombe Airport have night lighting for after-dark operations?
A: The airport has limited infrastructure typical of Madagascar's regional airfields, and most scheduled flights operate during daylight hours only.

Q: Is Wi-Fi available at the terminal?
A: Wi-Fi and other modern terminal amenities are generally not available; travelers should expect very basic facilities at this regional airport.
transport_tips: Getting to and from Morombe Airport is typically done by taxi or shared vehicle, as the terminal is located just outside the town center along the coast. Due to the limited flight schedule, pre-arranging ground transport with your hotel or a local contact is strongly recommended. Roads from Toliara to Morombe can be rough, so flying is often the preferred option for travelers short on time.
local_tip: The town of Morombe is famous for its traditional Vezo fishing culture, and the weekly fish market early in the morning is one of the most authentic cultural experiences in southwest Madagascar—time your arrival to catch it, as flights often land in the late morning.
